product.one_liner: Citely is an AI citation checker and source finder that helps users verify references, detect fake citations, and trace claims back to real sources.

core_features.description: Find original sources behind claims, references, or citation-like text.
core_features.user_benefit: Helps users trace claims back to real sources instead of trusting vague citations.
core_features.visual_need: Screen recording of pasting a claim or citation and getting source results.

core_features.description: Check whether references correspond to real published sources.
core_features.user_benefit: Helps users catch fake, incorrect, or mismatched references before submission.
core_features.visual_need: Screen recording of checking a reference list and seeing verification results.

core_features.description: Compare title, authors, year, journal, DOI, and other citation metadata.
core_features.user_benefit: Helps users identify references that look real but contain wrong details.
core_features.visual_need: Close-up screen recording of citation metadata comparison.

core_features.description: Check citations that may have been generated by AI tools.
core_features.user_benefit: Helps users avoid trusting AI-generated citations just because they look formatted.
core_features.visual_need: Screen recording of an AI-generated reference being checked.

most_painful_user_scenarios: A student uses AI to generate references but is not sure whether they are real.
A citation looks real but points to the wrong paper.
A researcher needs to verify references before submitting a manuscript.
A user wants to find the original source behind a claim.
forbidden_claims: Do not say Citely guarantees 100% citation accuracy.
Do not say Citely replaces human academic judgment.
Do not say Citely guarantees manuscript acceptance.
Do not say Citely can verify every possible source in the world.
Do not encourage users to submit unchecked AI-generated work.
Do not claim that a verified citation automatically means the argument is correct.
good_tiktok_angles: Before you trust an AI-generated reference, check this.
A citation can look real and still be fake.
This is the last step before I trust any AI-written research draft.
Don’t submit references before checking this.

reference_hook_summary: Reference opens with a close vertical selfie of a student covering their mouth in anxious disbelief, then cuts to a handheld laptop proof/report with finger pointing.

observation.camera: front-facing phone camera, subtle handheld movement, native TikTok feel

viral_pattern_card.script_formula: [authority/teacher thinks X] + [tiny reason or unfair suspicion] + [but I have tool/workflow proof showing Y]

reuse_rules: Keep the anxious student confession energy.
Do not copy the original creator identity or exact face.
Do not claim guaranteed detector bypass or academic misconduct.
Replace GPTZero report proof with each product’s truthful workflow proof.
Use hand/finger product footage after the hook whenever available.
